stops.name: The Sea of Galilee, walking on the water
stops.campa: He sends the disciples ahead by boat and goes up alone into a mountain to pray. In the fourth watch of the night, the boat tossed with waves and the wind contrary, he comes to them walking upon the sea. They are terrified, crying out for a ghost; but he says, Be of good cheer, it is I; be not afraid. Peter answers, Lord, bid me come; and he steps out onto the water and walks toward Jesus, until, seeing the wind, he is afraid and begins to sink and cries, Lord, save me. Jesus stretches out his hand and catches him, and the wind ceases.
stops.quote: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

stops.name: Caesarea Philippi (Banias), Peter's confession
stops.campa: At the foot of Hermon, by the springs of the Jordan and the great rock-shrine of Pan, Jesus asks his disciples, Whom do men say that I am? Some say John, some Elias, some Jeremias. But whom say ye that I am? Simon Peter answers, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God. Blessed art thou, Simon, for flesh and blood has not revealed this, but my Father. Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church. From here Jesus begins to tell them plainly that he must go up to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed, and rise the third day.
stops.quote: Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

stops.name: Mount Tabor, the Transfiguration
stops.campa: After six days he takes Peter, James, and John up into a high mountain apart, and is transfigured before them: his face shines as the sun, and his raiment becomes white as the light. Moses and Elias appear, talking with him of his coming departure at Jerusalem. Peter, half-asleep and bewildered, offers to build three tabernacles. Then a bright cloud overshadows them, and out of the cloud a voice speaks the same word heard at the Jordan. The disciples fall on their faces, sore afraid; Jesus touches them: Arise, be not afraid. And they see no man save Jesus only.
stops.quote: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.

stops.name: Bethany, the raising of Lazarus
stops.campa: Lazarus, whom he loves, has died and lain four days in the tomb. Martha meets him: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. Jesus weeps. Then he comes to the grave, a cave with a stone against it, and bids them take the stone away, though Martha warns of the stench. Lifting his eyes he gives thanks, then cries with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And the dead man comes out, bound hand and foot with graveclothes. Loose him, and let him go. Many believe; and this last and greatest sign hardens the council against him.
stops.quote: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the woman taken in adultery
stops.campa: In the Temple at dawn the scribes and Pharisees bring a woman taken in adultery and set her in the midst, to tempt him: Moses commanded to stone such; what sayest thou? Jesus stoops and writes with his finger on the ground, as though he heard them not. When they press him, he lifts himself and speaks one sentence, then stoops again. Convicted by their own conscience, they go out one by one, the eldest first, until she is left alone with him. Neither do I condemn thee, he tells her; go, and sin no more. Mercy without excuse, and judgment turned back on the judges.
stops.quote: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.

stops.name: Jericho, Zacchaeus and blind Bartimaeus
stops.campa: Passing through Jericho on the way up to Jerusalem, blind Bartimaeus sits begging by the road and cries out, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me; and Jesus restores his sight, for his faith has made him whole. And Zacchaeus, chief among the publicans and small of stature, climbs a sycamore tree to see him. Jesus looks up: Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must abide at thy house. The crowd murmurs that he goes to a sinner, but Zacchaeus repents and gives half his goods to the poor, and salvation comes to that house.
stops.quote: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

stops.name: Bethany, the anointing at Simon's house
stops.campa: Six days before the Passover, at supper in Bethany, Mary takes a pound of very costly ointment of pure nard and anoints his feet and wipes them with her hair, and the house is filled with the fragrance. Judas objects: it might have been sold and given to the poor, for he keeps the bag and is a thief. But Jesus defends her: Let her alone; against the day of my burying she has kept this. The poor ye have always, but me ye have not always. She has anointed his body beforehand for the grave; wheresoever the Gospel is preached, this shall be told for a memorial of her.
stops.quote: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.

stops.name: Bethphage, the entry into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday
stops.campa: At Bethphage on the Mount of Olives he sends for a colt whereon never man sat, and rides down toward the city as the prophet foretold: the king coming meek and lowly. A great multitude spreads garments and palm branches in the way, and the whole crowd cries Hosanna to the son of David. When he draws near and sees the city, he weeps over it, for it knows not the day of its visitation. The Pharisees bid him rebuke his disciples; he answers that if these hold their peace, the very stones would cry out.
stops.quote: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the cleansing of the Temple
stops.campa: He goes into the Temple and finds it a marketplace: the money-changers at their tables, sellers of oxen and sheep and doves. He makes a scourge of small cords, overthrows the tables, pours out the changers' money, and drives them all out, saying his Father's house has been made a den of thieves. The blind and the lame come to him in the Temple, and he heals them. The chief priests, seeing the wonders and the children crying Hosanna, are indignant and seek how they might destroy him, but fear the people, for all hang on his words.
stops.quote: It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

stops.name: The Cenacle, Mount Zion, the Last Supper
stops.campa: In a large upper room, furnished and prepared, he keeps the Passover with the Twelve. He rises from supper, girds himself with a towel, and washes their feet: the Lord and Master kneeling before his servants. Then, as they eat, he takes bread, blesses and breaks it: Take, eat, this is my body. And the cup: This is my blood of the new testament, shed for many. Do this in remembrance of me. He foretells that one of them will betray him and that Peter will deny him thrice before cockcrow, and gives them a new commandment: that they love one another.
stops.quote: This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

stops.name: Gethsemane, the Agony in the Garden
stops.campa: He comes with them to a garden at the foot of Olivet called Gethsemane, and begins to be sorrowful and very heavy: my soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death. He goes a stone's cast apart, falls on his face, and prays that the cup might pass; yet not my will but thine be done. His sweat becomes as it were great drops of blood falling to the ground, and an angel from heaven strengthens him. Thrice he finds the disciples sleeping. Then Judas comes with a band and lanterns and kisses him; and by that sign they take him and bind him.
stops.quote: O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.

stops.name: Jerusalem: before Caiaphas, and Peter's denial
stops.campa: They lead him to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the council seeks false witness to put him to death. When the high priest adjures him, art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? Jesus answers, I am, and ye shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds. Caiaphas rends his clothes, crying blasphemy, and they spit on him and buffet him. Below in the courtyard, warming himself at the fire, Peter thrice denies that he knows him; and the cock crows, and Peter, meeting the Lord's look, goes out and weeps bitterly.
stops.quote: I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
